topic: Elections and Electoral System — Election Commission, FPTP, EVM, delimitation
description: Election Commission of India (Art 324), First Past The Post system, Rajya Sabha elections (STV), VVPAT, Delimitation Commission, Model Code of Conduct — IBPS PO/SSC CGL/UPSC format.

questions.stem: The Election Commission of India derives its authority from which Article of the Constitution?

options.option_text: Article 324 — vests superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission
Article 280 — this establishes the Finance Commission, not the Election Commission
Article 315 — this deals with Public Service Commissions (UPSC/SPSC), not elections
Article 148 — this deals with the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, not elections

questions.explanation: ARTICLE 324: establishes the ELECTION COMMISSION OF INDIA (ECI). Functions: superintendence, direction, and control of preparation of electoral rolls and conduct of elections to Parliament, state legislatures, President, and Vice-President. COMPOSITION: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) + such number of Election Commissioners as the President may from time to time fix (currently 2 Election Commissioners = total 3 members). CEC REMOVAL: only by a procedure like that for removal of a SC judge — by Parliament on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity (Art 324(5)). INDEPENDENCE: ECI is a constitutional body insulated from executive interference. Election Commissioners also protected (1989 amendment). RECENT LAW: Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act 2023 — appointment by 3-member committee (PM, Home Minister, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha). PYQ FREQUENCY: Art 324 + ECI composition in IBPS PO, SSC CGL, UPSC Prelims — 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Lok Sabha elections in India use the First Past The Post (FPTP) electoral system. A key feature of FPTP is:

options.option_text: The candidate with the most votes wins, even without an absolute majority of votes cast
Seats are allocated to parties in proportion to their total national vote share
Voters rank candidates in order of preference; the winner must cross a quota
A second round (runoff) is held if no candidate wins more than 50% in the first round

questions.explanation: FPTP (FIRST PAST THE POST) / SINGLE MEMBER PLURALITY: the candidate with the MOST VOTES (plurality) wins — even if they get only 30% of votes. No need for an absolute majority (>50%). WHY USED IN INDIA: simple to understand, quick results, strong constituency-representative link. WEAKNESS: 'Wasted votes' — if 3 candidates split 40-35-25%, the 40% candidate wins despite 60% voting against them. 'Manufactured majorities' — a party with 40% national vote can get 60%+ seats. PROPORTIONAL REPRESENTATION (option B): used in Rajya Sabha elections and Presidential elections (by STV). PREFERENTIAL VOTING (option C): used in Irish elections and Rajya Sabha/Presidential elections (Single Transferable Vote = STV). RUNOFF SYSTEM (option D): used in France and several other countries for Presidential elections. FPTP USED IN: Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, local body elections. PYQ FREQUENCY: FPTP feature + comparison in SSC CGL, IBPS PO, UPSC Prelims — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Rajya Sabha members are elected by:

options.option_text: Elected members of each State Legislative Assembly using the Single Transferable Vote (STV) method
Direct election by all registered voters of a state — similar to how Lok Sabha MPs are elected
Nomination by the President on the advice of the Chief Minister of each state
Members of the State Legislative Council only, in states where such councils exist

questions.explanation: RAJYA SABHA ELECTIONS (Art 80): elected by elected members of STATE LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLIES (not Legislative Councils, not by the people directly) using PROPORTIONAL REPRESENTATION with SINGLE TRANSFERABLE VOTE (STV). STV/PR: each state gets seats proportional to its population. Voters (MLAs) rank candidates; votes are transferred if a candidate exceeds the quota or is eliminated. ELECTED vs NOMINATED: 238 members elected (12 from each UT with legislature, rest from states); 12 NOMINATED by President (distinguished persons in arts, literature, science, social service). TERM: 6 years (not coterminous with Lok Sabha); 1/3 retire every 2 years. OPTION B wrong: Rajya Sabha is elected INDIRECTLY (by MLAs), not directly by voters. OPTION C wrong: President nominates only 12 members; the rest are elected. OPTION D wrong: State Legislative Councils are state-level (Vidhan Parishad) and have no role in electing RS members. PYQ FREQUENCY: Rajya Sabha election method in IBPS PO, SSC CGL, UPSC Prelims — 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: The Model Code of Conduct (MCC) enforced by the Election Commission of India during elections is:

options.option_text: A non-statutory convention — voluntary but strictly enforced by ECI using its Art 324 powers
A statutory law enacted by Parliament — violating it is a criminal offence under the IPC
A presidential ordinance issued before every election — it lapses after the results are declared
A part of the Constitution since the 61st Amendment — it has the status of a fundamental duty

questions.explanation: MODEL CODE OF CONDUCT (MCC): a set of guidelines issued by the Election Commission of India for political parties and candidates during election periods. STATUS: NOT a statute or law — it is based on CONSENSUS and CONVENTION, enforced by the ECI using its constitutional authority under Art 324. Violation is dealt with by censure, show-cause notices, and reporting to the President/Governor — not by criminal prosecution under the MCC itself (though specific actions may violate other laws). ENFORCEMENT: comes into effect from the date of announcement of the election schedule till the date of declaration of results. APPLIES TO: all candidates, political parties, AND the incumbent government (which cannot announce new schemes, inaugurate projects, or use government machinery for campaigning during MCC period). ORIGIN: first developed in 1960 for Kerala elections; gradually refined; widely used from 1979 onwards. EXAMPLE PROVISIONS: no use of religious appeal to voters, no bribery, government cannot announce new welfare schemes after MCC kicks in. PYQ FREQUENCY: MCC non-statutory nature in UPSC Prelims, SSC CGL, IBPS PO — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: The Delimitation Commission redraws constituency boundaries in India. The last delimitation exercise effective for Lok Sabha elections was based on:

options.option_text: 2001 Census data — Delimitation Commission Act 2002; effective from 2008 elections
2011 Census data — delimitation was due after 2011 but has been constitutionally deferred
1971 Census data — an earlier delimitation, but not the most recently effective exercise
1991 Census data — delimitation done in the 1990s was the last effective one for Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: DELIMITATION IN INDIA: CURRENT SITUATION: Under the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976), the number of Lok Sabha seats (543) and their demarcation were FROZEN until the first Census after 2001 (i.e., 2001 Census). DELIMITATION COMMISSION ACT 2002: constituted the Delimitation Commission which used 2001 Census data. Its orders were effective from 2008 (the 2009 Lok Sabha election was the first using the redrawn boundaries). FURTHER FREEZE: Article 82 was amended so that the next delimitation will be after the first Census post-2026. Given the 2021 Census was delayed (COVID), the next delimitation will be based on the 2031 Census at the earliest. 1971 Census: the 45th Amendment froze the number of seats based on 1971 Census (seat count didn't change 1977-2008, only boundaries were redrawn using 2001 data). OPTION B: Although delimitation using 2011 Census was due, it has been deferred until post-2026 (Art 82, 84 as amended). PYQ FREQUENCY: delimitation commission + 2001 census in UPSC Prelims, SSC CGL, IBPS PO polity — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: VVPAT (Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail) was made mandatory for all constituencies in Indian general elections following a Supreme Court direction in:

options.option_text: 2013 — and first used comprehensively in all constituencies in the 2019 General Election
2004 — VVPAT was introduced along with EVMs for all constituencies in 2004 elections
2009 — the UPA government mandated VVPAT as part of its electoral reforms package
1998 — experimental use began alongside EVMs in their very first nationwide deployment

questions.explanation: VVPAT: after a voter presses a button on the EVM, a printed paper slip (showing the candidate's name, symbol) appears behind a glass window for 7 seconds, then drops into a sealed compartment. HISTORY: Subramanian Swamy & others petitioned the SC to mandate VVPAT. Supreme Court ordered in 2013 (PUCL v. Union of India) that VVPAT must be used. ROLLOUT: gradually expanded. Fully deployed in ALL constituencies for the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. EVM TIMELINE: first experimental use in 1982 (Paravur, Kerala); first full national election 1999 (though some constituencies in 1998 used EVMs). 2019 VVPAT VERIFICATION: SC allowed 5 VVPAT slips to be counted per assembly segment (out of demand for 50%). POST-2024: after 2024 Lok Sabha election petitions, SC maintained the existing 5-slip sampling as statistically sufficient. OPTION B wrong: EVMs were widely introduced in 1999, not VVPAT. PYQ FREQUENCY: VVPAT mandate year in UPSC Prelims, IBPS PO, SSC CGL polity GA — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: The 'Anti-defection Law' in India (10th Schedule, added by 52nd Amendment 1985) disqualifies a legislator who:

options.option_text: Voluntarily gives up membership of the political party that sponsored their election
Votes against the government on a confidence motion even once during their term
Misses more than 10 consecutive sessions of the legislature without prior permission
Files nomination papers for another party's election without resigning the current seat

questions.explanation: 10TH SCHEDULE (ANTI-DEFECTION LAW, 52nd AMENDMENT 1985): added by Rajiv Gandhi government to prevent 'aaya ram, gaya ram' phenomenon (frequent defections for money/ministerial positions). GROUNDS FOR DISQUALIFICATION: (1) VOLUNTARILY GIVES UP membership of the party on whose ticket elected. (2) VOTES/ABSTAINS AGAINST party whip in the legislature (unless 15+ days' prior permission given). EXCEPTION — MERGER: a legislator is NOT disqualified if 2/3 of the party's legislative members merge with another party (merger exemption). DECISION AUTHORITY: Speaker/Chairman of the house (their decision is subject to judicial review — Kihoto Hollohan case, 1992). OPTION B: Voting against a confidence motion alone doesn't trigger it — only if the party has issued a WHIP and the member defied it. The whip must be explicit. OPTION C: absenteeism is a separate matter under rules of procedure, not 10th Schedule. UPSC ANGLE: criticism of anti-defection law — Speaker as arbiter has faced charges of partisan decisions; demand for neutral tribunal. PYQ FREQUENCY: Anti-defection grounds in SSC CGL, IBPS PO, UPSC Prelims — 1-2× per cycle.
